rubrics.date: Rubricae generales 10–12 and 15–18 (Vatican typical edition, p. [XII]), with the table at 91 (places 4, 6, 11 and 15, p. XVII): a first-class feast of the universal Church that is not a feast of the Lord takes the place of a second-class Sunday, and the Immaculate Conception that of the Second Sunday of Advent (15), and the Sunday is commemorated; a feast of the Lord and the feasts of 17 take a Sunday's place with no commemoration of it (16 a, 17, 112 b, p. XVIII). The Sunday commemorated is the one the calendar would have kept that day, a Sunday after Epiphany resumed after the Twenty-third Sunday after Pentecost included (18).
rubrics.scope: Observed in the Mass of the feast by the impeded Sunday's own Collect, Secret and Postcommunion, as that Sunday's formulary assembles them; the Mass of an impeded Sunday is neither anticipated nor resumed (Rubricae generales 14, p. [XII]).
rubrics.rank: Rubricae generales 108–109 a (p. XVIII): the commemoration of a Sunday is privileged and is made in all Masses.
rubrics.admission: Rubricae generales 111 a and 434 a (pp. XVIII, XXXI): a first-class day, and a sung Mass that is not conventual, admit one privileged commemoration; 113 (p. XIX): a de Tempore commemoration comes first.
rubrics.conclusion: Rubricae generales 436–437 (p. XXXI): each commemoration oration follows the corresponding Mass oration under its own, separate conclusion; 480–481: only the last Secret's terminal is audible.
